props.gloss_en: R' Meir: one may not sell [a holy thing] of the many to an individual
R' Meir's ground: because they lower it from its sanctity
the Sages to R' Meir: if so, [one could] not even [sell] from a large town to a small town
from a large town to a small town: at the outset it was holy, now too it is holy
from the many to an individual: there is no sanctity
if there is reason for concern, in a case like this [large town to small] too there is reason for concern
because of 'in the multitude of people is the king's glory' (Mishlei 14:28)

objections.gloss_en: שפיר קאמרי ליה רבנן לרבי מאיר! -- the Sages' 'if so, not even from a large town to a small one' is well said against R' Meir

answered_by.gloss_en: ורבי מאיר: מעיר גדולה לעיר קטנה -- מעיקרא קדישא, השתא נמי קדישא; מרבים ליחיד ליכא קדושה -- the town-to-town case keeps its sanctity, the sale to an individual does not
